title: The waveform's fractal dimension: Petrosian FD (a newly-authored op), bit-for-bit against antropy

dataset.name: EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb)
dataset.record: subject S002, run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples); spatial map uses all 64 channels
dataset.citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: The Petrosian fractal dimension (1995) is a fast waveform-complexity index: it counts the sign changes in a signal's derivative (the density of local extrema) -- a smooth oscillation scores near 1, a complex signal higher. The ecosystem's complexity suite (permutation entropy, Lempel-Ziv, Hjorth, sample/approximate entropy, DFA, RQA, SVD entropy) lacked this waveform-fractal view; this case introduces a NEWLY-AUTHORED op, petrosianFD. On a real eyes-closed posterior EEG channel it reproduces antropy.petrosian_fd BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| 0), and the finding: Petrosian FD is lower over the posterior alpha region (all 9 parieto-occipital channels below the frontal mean) -- the eyes-closed alpha rhythm is a smoother, more regular oscillation.

claims.statement: Petrosian fractal dimension of the posterior channel POz -- waveform-complexity index
samples in the analyzed channel (10 s at 160 Hz)
mean Petrosian FD over the posterior (parieto-occipital) channels
mean Petrosian FD over the frontal channels -- higher (more complex waveform)
posterior channels (of 9) with Petrosian FD below the frontal mean -- robustness of the smoother-posterior finding

validation.reference: The newly-authored petrosianFD op is validated against antropy.petrosian_fd. antropy re-computes the Petrosian fractal dimension from the same signal; the agreement is BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| 0) because the closed-form formula P = log10(N)/(log10(N)+log10(N/(N+0.4*Nd))) and the derivative-sign-change count Nd (np.signbit convention: values < 0) are identical. The finding: Petrosian FD is lower over the posterior alpha region (all 9 posterior channels below the frontal mean; posterior 1.020 vs frontal 1.027).
validation.data: REAL -- eegmmidb (PhysioNet), subject S002 run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz for the certified op; all 64 channels for the spatial map
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) the newly-authored petrosianFD reproduces antropy.petrosian_fd bit-for-bit (max |diff| 0); (2) Petrosian FD is lower over the posterior alpha region (9/9 posterior channels below the frontal mean). HONEST scope: (1) this op is NEWLY AUTHORED to fill a gap -- the complexity suite (permutation entropy, Lempel-Ziv, Hjorth, sample/approximate entropy, DFA, RQA, SVD entropy) lacked the waveform-fractal-dimension view; (2) this is a genuine MACHINE-PRECISION match -- the op and antropy compute the IDENTICAL closed-form Petrosian FD with the same derivative-sign-change count, so the residual is exactly 0, not a convention agreement (unlike the Higuchi/Katz fractal dimensions, whose conventions differ across tools); (3) the finding -- lower Petrosian FD posteriorly -- indicates the eyes-closed alpha rhythm is a smoother, more regular oscillation (fewer local extrema), consistent with the SVD-entropy/Welch/Hjorth/coherence cases on the SAME data; a descriptive spatial pattern on one subject/segment, not a clinical claim; (4) run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: The Petrosian FD is a coarse waveform-complexity index (near 1 for most physiological signals); pairing it with SVD entropy, Hjorth, and the fractal exponents (DFA) on the same beats/epochs -- and contrasting eyes-closed vs eyes-open -- would show which complexity facet best tracks the alpha rhythm's appearance. Documented, not escalated.
